metadata.note: The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit is the passenger rail Morgantown has today, and the only one it has had since 1953. Automated rubber-tyred cars on an elevated guideway link WVU's downtown and Evansdale campuses: Walnut, Beechurst, Engineering, Towers and Medical. Phase I (Walnut - Engineering) opened in 1975; Phase II (on to Medical) during the 1978-79 school year. It is drawn as two features so each half appears in the year it opened. Mode is recorded as rapid_transit - it is a grade-separated automated guideway system, closest in character to the other rapid_transit layers here, though OSM tags it railway=monorail.
not_yet_sourced: the exact opening date of Phase II (drawn from 1979)
published headways - the 5-minute figure is the peak dispatch interval, not a timetabled headway
seasonal closure is noted but not modelled: the PRT does not run over the summer or normally on Sundays

segments.note: The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit, built for WVU with federal funding as a demonstration of automated small-vehicle transit, opened in 1975 with three stations - Walnut (downtown), Beechurst and Engineering. Rubber-tyred driverless cars run on a dedicated concrete guideway; on demand off-peak, and dispatched on headways of roughly five minutes when waiting builds at peak. It still runs, carrying about 16,000 riders a day during term, and a renewal project approved in 2012 has been replacing the control system and the fleet. Note that it runs term-time only (roughly 6:30am-10:15pm weekdays, normally closed Sundays and over the summer).
sources: Segment-level: the 1975 Phase I opening with three stations, the 30 mph maximum, the ~5-minute peak dispatch interval and the 2012 renewal are from the Wikipedia article on the Morgantown PRT and WVU's own PRT pages.

segments.note: Phase II, opened during the 1978-79 academic year, carried the guideway on from Engineering past Towers to Medical, at the Health Sciences Center - the northern end of the present five-station system. End to end, Walnut to Medical takes 11.5 minutes.
sources: Segment-level: the Phase II 1978-79 extension, the five-station order and the 11.5-minute end-to-end time are from the Wikipedia article on the Morgantown PRT. The 1979 start year is this dataset's reading of 'expanded during the 1978-1979 school year'; the exact opening date is NOT sourced.
